I’m using the repository’s `crimes-codebase-risk` review workflow to classify the scan findings against the actual IA surfaces, with emphasis on user-facing reachability and access-control risk.

The skill file lives at the evaluation workspace level rather than this runner directory; I’m resolving that path, then I’ll verify only the files implicated by the IA findings.

The scan has no `high` findings, so there is no automatic severity-based gate. However, the evidence shows two concrete IA clusters I would treat as blocking quality.

| Finding | Assessment | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `permission_ia_drift` (`crime_00010`) | **Blocker** | `/admin` uses three incompatible role models: nav requires `admin`, docs say `manager`, and the route declares `owner` while still allowing `manager`. This can produce incorrect visibility or access behavior. See [src/nav.ts](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/d0b4a6f6-acd0-4986-8afe-011e15f736b2/scratchpad/evalwt/evals/fixtures/05-stress-ia-drift/src/nav.ts:10), [docs/routes.md](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/d0b4a6f6-acd0-4986-8afe-011e15f736b2/scratchpad/evalwt/evals/fixtures/05-stress-ia-drift/docs/routes.md:12), and [src/routes/admin.ts](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/d0b4a6f6-acd0-4986-8afe-011e15f736b2/scratchpad/evalwt/evals/fixtures/05-stress-ia-drift/src/routes/admin.ts:4). |
| `parallel_destination` plus billing orphans (`crime_00003`, `00005`, `00006`) | **Blocker if billing is shipped; I would block now** | Docs advertise `/billing-plan`, while code contains `/billing-plans` and `/admin/billing-plans`; neither code destination is linked from nav or docs. There is no defensible canonical billing journey. If billing is intentionally unreleased, remove it from the docs and track consolidation as a follow-up. |
| Workspace/organisation orphans (`crime_00007`, `00008`) | **Blocker for a production nav** | Nav points to plural `/workspaces` and `/organisations`, while route files and docs use singular `/workspace` and `/organisation`. In a file-based route scheme, the nav likely points at nonexistent destinations. Resolve the URL contract or add explicit redirects. |
| `concept_alias_drift` (`crime_00002`) | **Follow-up in isolation** | `team`, `workspace`, and `organisation` may represent one tenant concept—or legitimately distinct concepts. Don’t blindly rename them from this finding alone. Document the domain model, then choose canonical labels. The singular/plural URL inconsistencies above remain concrete issues regardless. |
| `docs_code_drift` (`crime_00011`) | **False positive / non-blocking** | `/admin` is an application URL backed by `src/routes/admin.ts`, not a filesystem-relative documentation link. Record feedback rather than changing the valid link: `crimes feedback 'docs_code_drift::docs/routes.md::' --verdict fp --note '/admin is an application route implemented by src/routes/admin.ts, not a filesystem documentation path'` |
| CLI command drift (`crime_00012`) | **Follow-up, outside IA scope** | The documented `iaq teams`, `iaq workspace`, and `iaq refresh` commands are stale, but this does not determine route/nav consistency. It should still be corrected before publishing those CLI docs. |
| Action/copy label drift (`crime_00004`, `00009`) | **Follow-up, outside requested files** | `archive`, `delete`, and `remove` occur in component actions. Standardize after confirming whether they really have identical semantics. |

Recommended resolution: establish one route matrix shared by code, nav, and docs; select a single billing destination; centralize the `/admin` permission policy; then add a test that every nav destination resolves and that documented routes match the route registry. The missing-agent-context and dependency-provenance findings are unrelated to this IA review.
